newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin, officials say Chechnya stays Russian.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin, officials say Chechnya stays Russian.

text.p: Top Russian officials convened by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Saturday renewed Moscow's insistence that a final peace deal with Chechen separatists must ensure that the region remains an integral part of Russia.

"In the course of the meeting it was stressed that the resolution of all these complex issues must be based only on the constitution of the Russian Federation and on the principle of the territorial integrity of Russia," the government press service said in a statement.

It said Chernomyrdin, who has taken on some responsibilities from Boris Yeltsin while the president prepares for heart surgery, had charged certain officials with new tasks aimed at a lasting settlement following the peace deal signed by Kremlin security chief Alexander Lebed on August 31.

Lebed, who spoke at the meeting, agreed with the rebels to withdraw Russian troops and defer for five years the resolution of the separatists' demands for independence. Chernomyrdin has stressed the deal is not legally binding and ministers have said they are worried Lebed did not do enough to rule out secession.
Saturday's meeting discussed the formation of a transitional regional government for Chechnya, tightening up security in the and ensuring the release of people held captive there.

The officials decided to hold weekly meetings, a move that appeared close to resurrecting the defunct committee on Chechnya, chaired by Chernomyrdin, which Yeltsin disbanded last month when he put Lebed in sole charge of ending the conflict.

Lebed, an ambitious political outsider was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying: "It is essential to decide with collective wisdom which steps should be taken to settle the Chechen crisis after the signing of the Khasav-Yurt accords."
Lebed signed the deal at Khasav-Yurt, just outside Chechnya.
Chernomyrdin gave it a cool response, insisting it was a political "statement of intention" and not a legal treaty.
With Yeltsin sidelined by his forthcoming surgery, there is speculation on a power struggle in the Kremlin involving Chernomyrdin and Lebed among others.
The 65-year-old president was spending the weekend in a Moscow clinic for more pre-surgical checks.

His influential chief-of-staff, Anatoly Chubais, was at the meeting, as were the chief of the Russian general staff and the justice minister among others. The defence and interior ministers did not appear in film of the start of the meeting.

In Chechnya, a three-way conflict has been brewing between Russian troops, the separatist rebels who seized the capital Grozny last month and the pro-Moscow Chechen administration, which Lebed pointedly left out of his peace settlement.
